submit_request.description: One ordinary producer Event with the approval signatures its two approval layers require for the Event action or for this registered submit operation, or one atomic MLS Commit plus all recipient Welcome deliveries required by that Commit. The ordinary branch is EventCommitSubmission itself, not a second declaration of it: the approval evidence a constraint demands has to be carriable on the primary ingress, otherwise no execution could ever satisfy the constraint (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.5).

self_submit_request.description: Closed self Event-submit union. Ordinary Event and MLS Commit requests retain their current canonical shapes. Direct Conversation founding and membership compensation are the only aggregate branches; both are closed and are rejected on every other Event-submit endpoint.

self_submit_outcome.description: Closed self Event-submit outcome union. Aggregate outcomes cannot be parsed as an ordinary single-Event outcome.

peer_submit_request.description: The only peer Event ingress. branch is a semantic discriminator, not a routing hint: authority_forward performs first admission at the current governance Station; committed_replication stores source-committed replicas; registered_atomic_unit performs one registered all-or-nothing materialization. Bodies cannot be reinterpreted across branches.

peer_submit_outcome.description: Closed peer Event-submit outcome union. Replication reports one same-order item result for every input; registered units report exactly one indivisible outcome.

committed_event_submission.description: One full producer submission paired with the source-signed RealmCommit that accepted it. submission.event.event_id MUST equal source_commit.event_ref; realm and stream coordinates, governance generation, current source authority signature and previous_commit_ref continuity MUST verify exactly. This shape never accepts EventReadRow, redacted Event views or locked stubs.

replicated_committed_event_submission.description: One committed-replication item. The receiver verifies the exact source Event/Commit pair plus destination membership, route and history/plaintext visibility at the source commit basis. It then stores those exact source bytes; it MUST NOT perform first admission, sign another RealmCommit, or enqueue a second federation fanout.

recipient_witnesses.description: Canonical bytewise-sorted unique witnesses. The authenticated destination service MUST equal every recipient_service_id selected for this request, each member route must resolve to that service, and current membership/history/plaintext visibility must authorize this exact source commit.

peer_committed_replication_outcome.description: Per-item replication outcome. results has exactly the same length and order as request.submissions. A stored or duplicate row names the exact source coordinates; rejected means that item was not stored. Transport retry replays the complete request body and returns the same results. This branch has no accepted finality vocabulary.

direct_conversation_founding_unit_submis.description: Self-only caller-authored Direct Conversation founding unit. The current Station recomputes authority from current evidence and therefore rejects a founding_authority_evidence echo. The four Events are accepted atomically in this exact order with consecutive RealmCommits: realm create, founder join, peer join, strand create. realm_id is retyped from events[0].event.event_id and main_strand_id from events[3].event.event_id.

idempotency_key.description: UUIDv7 founding-slot fence. Byte-identical replay returns the same four byte-identical source RealmCommits without changing the fourth committed_at; the same key with different canonical unit bytes is duplicate_conflict.

allOf.description: payload action MUST be join. The first occurrence is the founder and the second is the peer; the pair and Realm bindings must match the realm-create Event.

direct_conversation_founding_federation_.description: Peer-only source-committed Direct Conversation founding unit. The four committed rows have the same Event order as the self unit; their source commits have one Realm/generation/stream, consecutive positions and exact previous_commit_ref linkage. The receiver derives every coordinate from the four Events, verifies the source commits and bounded authority evidence, then materializes all four rows or none without re-signing commits or creating fanout. No second acceptance receipt or finality object exists.

direct_conversation_founding_acceptance_.description: One indivisible Direct Conversation founding outcome. Self first success, peer success and exact replay return the same four verified source commits. The commits are ordered like the unit and form one consecutive source chain; the fourth committed_at is the founding acceptance time. No receipt or per-item partial result exists.

peer_registered_atomic_unit.description: Closed registry of peer source-committed atomic units. Every listed unit is persisted and materialized all-or-nothing and produces no new Arkret Event finality.

membership_compensation_unit_submission.description: Self-only membership compensation aggregate. The enclosed Event is an ak.member.state leave/remove whose authorization_ref equals evidence.delegation.delegation_id. Evidence is transport-only and excluded from Event canonical bytes. The destination authority claims (admission_id, delegation_id) once in the same transaction as Event acceptance; mismatch, already absent, prior use or a superseding J2/new join is membership_compensation_conflict with zero writes.

membership_compensation_federation_submi.description: Peer-only source-committed membership compensation unit. The receiver verifies the full source Event/Commit pair and the unchanged compensation evidence, then atomically claims the same single-use binding and stores the source fact without re-signing a commit or fanout.

membership_compensation_evidence.description: Closed transport-only compensation evidence. The verifier recomputes delegation_id as ak:membership_compensation_delegation:sha256:<lowercase_hex SHA-256(JCS(core))>, verifies both signatures and exact join/admission/commit/executor bindings, and compares single_use_binding byte-for-byte. It is never inserted into Event canonical bytes.

membership_compensation_acceptance_outco.description: Atomic compensation outcome. committed and duplicate both carry the one authority-signed source commit. Exact full-body replay returns the same outcome; no per-item partial exists.

direct_conversation_founding_dependency_.description: Closed HTTP 409 application/problem+json response for a registered Direct Conversation founding unit whose bounded exact dependencies are not locally available. It is retryable only after canonical backfill/resolve and a new full-body request evaluation; no partial unit write occurred.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The closed endpoint problem retains the RFC literal type/title/status/detail/instance member vocabulary and adds one registered details member.

stream_scan_request.description: Positional single-stream scan request. Pagination is by stream_position, not by an opaque cursor: within one stream the governance Station's stream_position is a strict +1 total order, so the position IS the continuation token. Exactly one of after_position / before_position MUST be present; the exclusivity is structural (the oneOf below), so a request carrying both or neither is a schema violation and MUST NOT be repaired by picking a default direction. Both bounds are read inside the range this caller is permitted to read, never over the physical stream: null means 'from the oldest position this caller may read' (after_position) or 'from the newest position this caller may read' (before_position). Continuation is the caller's job: take the largest stream_position of this batch for after_position, the smallest for before_position.

after_position.description: Scan toward newer commits: return commits whose stream_position is strictly greater than this value, ascending. null starts at the oldest position this caller may read, which is position 0 only when that floor is the physical stream start; see stream_scan_outcome.readable_floor.

before_position.description: Scan toward older commits (history backfill): return commits whose stream_position is strictly smaller than this value, descending. null starts at the newest position this caller may read, which is not necessarily the physical stream head. The scan stops at the caller's readable floor; positions below that floor are unreadable rather than missing and are not a gap (zh/sync/client-sync.md section 12.3.3).

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of one caller's readable range on one stream. The anchor lets a member whose history is trimmed verify that its permitted prefix is complete without ever holding position 0: it proves where the accepted chain that caller may read begins, and it proves nothing about whether the Station holds further history below it or further updates above it.

oldest_position.description: Smallest stream_position this caller is permitted to read. Positions below it are unreadable, not missing: their absence MUST NOT be treated as a gap and MUST NOT be used to infer activity, membership or existence below the floor.

floor_commit_id.description: commit_id of the RealmCommit at oldest_position, so the boundary binds to the chain the caller has already accepted. The commit at the floor is the only readable commit allowed to carry a previous_commit_ref the caller cannot resolve, because its predecessor is outside that caller's range.

floor_reason.description: Why the range starts here. stream_start means the floor is the physical start of the stream and oldest_position is 0; the other three are trimmed ranges and MUST NOT be reported as stream_start.

stream_row.description: One committed row of a single stream: the RealmCommit and the Event it accepted. The row MUST be self-consistent: when the event member carries an event_id, that event_id MUST equal commit.event_ref, and a caller MUST reject the row instead of reconciling the two. Because commit.event_ref already names the source Event, a ReferenceLockedEventStub in this position MUST carry event_id; the stub's optional event_id exists for reference projections where the source event id itself is withheld, so the stub name is never by itself a privacy guarantee. Verifying the commit is not a reference-disclosure decision: a caller not permitted to know that the source Event exists MUST NOT receive this row at all, and a caller permitted to know it exists receives here the same redacted or locked projection it receives on every other read surface.

event.description: Committed event as delivered to this caller. A full EventEnvelope is the only reducer input shape; when the target Realm policy denies reference disclosure to this caller the row carries RedactedEventView or ReferenceLockedEventStub instead (zh/models/relation.md §4.5 Raw Event API boundary), which are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed to a reducer.

stream_scan_outcome.description: Positional scan result. There is no cursor and no has_more here: the caller continues from the largest (after_position) or smallest (before_position) stream_position of commits[]. Every boundary in this outcome is the caller's own permitted range: commits[] carries what this caller may read, truncated speaks only about further readable commits, and readable_floor names the verifiable bottom of that range.

commits.description: Contiguous commits of the requested stream, ordered by stream_position: ascending for after_position, descending for before_position. Callers MUST verify consecutive positions and previous_commit_ref linkage within and across pages. The linkage check is one equation in both directions, stated on adjacent positions rather than on array order: the row at the larger stream_position MUST carry previous_commit_ref equal to the commit_id of the row at the smaller position, whether that neighbour is the next or the previous element of this array and whether it arrived in this page or in the page before it. A descending page therefore keeps its last row as the anchor for the next page, and the commit at the caller's readable floor is the only readable commit whose predecessor the caller cannot check.

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of this caller's readable range on the requested stream. It MUST be present on every page whose scan reached that bottom (a before_position page with truncated false, and an after_position page whose first row is at it), MAY be present on any other page of the same stream, and MUST be omitted only when the caller may read no commit of this stream at all, which is also the only case in which an empty commits[] with truncated false is legal.

truncated.description: True when at least one further commit that this caller is permitted to read exists beyond this page in the requested direction, i.e. the scan stopped on limit. It is a statement about the caller's permitted range, never about the physical stream: a scan that stopped on the newest readable position (after_position) or on readable_floor.oldest_position (before_position) MUST set it false even when the Station holds further commits this caller may not read. History outside the caller's range MUST NOT set it, a page that stopped on the floor MUST NOT be presented as truncation, and truncated MUST NOT be used to conceal a floor. An empty commits[] with truncated false means the caller's permitted range is exhausted in that direction, never that the physical stream is empty or absent.

committed_event_ref.description: Closed exact reference to one authority-committed Event. All four coordinates are verified against the returned RealmCommit; none is a hint.

source_ref_access.description: Source-signed, Directory-bound authorization. The authenticated caller service MUST equal directory_id; realm_id MUST match this request; every requested ref MUST be a byte-identical member of source_refs.

refs.description: Canonical ascending unique refs. Every stream_ref realm_id equals the request realm_id and every ref is a byte-identical member of source_ref_access.source_refs.

items.description: Only exact matches, in request order. Callers fail closed when any requested ref is absent.

final_stream_heads.description: Private state-transfer manifest whose canonical digest equals handoff.final_stream_heads_digest. It is not included in the public authority bundle.
